objective: Create the two pure-Kotlin-JVM library modules of the Activity Ledger build: core-domain and core-wear-protocol. Both are plain Kotlin JVM modules -- they apply the `kotlin-jvm` plugin from the version catalog (alias libs.plugins.kotlin.jvm) and must NOT apply any Android plugin or declare an `android { }` block. Neither needs the Android framework, and keeping them off it makes them fast to unit-test and impossible to accidentally couple to platform types. Each module gets: a build.gradle.kts applying only the Kotlin JVM plugin and setting the JDK toolchain to 21 (read from the catalog's jdkToolchain version, not hardcoded); a package root directory under src/main/kotlin/; one minimal Kotlin source file whose only purpose is to prove the main source set compiles; and one minimal unit test under src/test/kotlin/ proving the test source set is wired and runs. Package roots: com.mcfrenchpants.activityledger.core.domain for core-domain, and com.mcfrenchpants.activityledger.core.wearprotocol for core-wear-protocol. Use `testImplementation(kotlin("test"))` for the test dependency -- it resolves at the applied Kotlin plugin's own version, so it introduces no new version into the catalog and needs no verification. The placeholder source file in each module must carry a comment stating plainly that it is a scaffold placeholder with no product meaning, to be deleted when real code lands in that module, so a later reader does not mistake it for domain modelling. Do not model any real domain concept: the canonical activity / raw capture / occurrence model belongs to a later backlog item, and inventing a stand-in now would create a fake precedent for it. core-wear-protocol is intended to hold only the phone/watch message contract -- data shapes and path constants -- so it must not depend on Play Services, on any Android type, or on any other project module. core-domain likewise must not depend on any other project module. This task is also the FIRST time any Gradle plugin is actually applied and resolved from a repository: the catalog's AGP/Kotlin/KSP plugin coordinates have never been exercised, because SS1.1 declared them all `apply false`. If the Kotlin 2.3.21 plugin marker fails to resolve, that is a real finding about the catalog, not a transient error -- report it with the exact Gradle error rather than substituting a different version. Kotlin MUST NOT be moved off 2.3.21: KSP has no 2.4.x release and Room requires KSP, so bumping Kotlin is a hard build break. Each module directory currently holds a .gitkeep created by SS1.1 to satisfy Gradle 9's requirement that an included project directory exist. Once a module has real tracked content you may delete its .gitkeep, but only in the two modules this task touches.
non_goals: Do not touch the other six modules (app-phone, app-wear, core-data, core-ai, core-speech, core-testing) or delete their .gitkeep files -- SS1.3 through SS1.5 own those.
Do not apply any Android Gradle Plugin, add an android { } block, or add any androidx / Play Services / ML Kit dependency to either module.
Do not model real product domain concepts (activities, captures, occurrences, corrections, aliases). Placeholders only.
Do not add any dependency beyond the Kotlin standard library and kotlin("test").
Do not add telemetry, analytics, crash reporting, or any logging of user content.
Do not modify settings.gradle.kts, the root build.gradle.kts, gradle.properties, or the Gradle wrapper -- SS1.1 settled those.
Do not edit anything under docs/, .sdlc/, agents/, scripts/, BACKLOG.md, PROGRESS.md, CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md.
acceptance_criteria: `./gradlew :core-domain:test :core-wear-protocol:test` is BUILD SUCCESSFUL and both modules' tests actually execute (a module with zero tests trivially 'passes' -- confirm real test execution, e.g. via the generated test report or --info, and state the evidence).

Neither module's build.gradle.kts applies an Android plugin or declares an `android { }` block, and neither declares a dependency on any other project module. Verifiable by reading both files and by `./gradlew :core-domain:dependencies :core-wear-protocol:dependencies`.
Both modules set the JDK toolchain to 21 by reading the version from gradle/libs.versions.toml rather than hardcoding the number.
The Kotlin 2.3.21 plugin marker actually resolved from a repository -- report the evidence. Kotlin's version is unchanged at 2.3.21 in the catalog.

gradle/libs.versions.toml is unchanged unless a change was genuinely required; if it changed, every added version must have been verified as actually resolving, and the report must state what was added and why.
The placeholder source file in each module carries a comment identifying it as a scaffold placeholder to be deleted when real code lands.
